purpose: Runtime policy for Milestone 8.1 adversarial review evidence (scripts/lib/adversarial-review-validator.ps1). Defines what an EXECUTION-REVIEW.json may claim, which claims Axiom-PMO can verify against external ground truth, and who may set which finding status. Design rationale and threat model: docs/architecture/adversarial-review.md.
core_principle: An EXECUTION-REVIEW.json is candidate evidence, never authority. A verdict recorded in it must never change a validator exit code, and it never substitutes for a human approval row in PROJECT.md -- the same standing pmo-config/handoff-policy.json already gives a semantic handoff review.

authority.note: AREV-* checks whether the artifact is structurally sound and whose provenance it carries. They never judge whether the review's content is thorough, correct, or intelligent -- that is not a deterministic question.

evidence_provenance._note: Reuses execution-contract-policy.json's evidence_provenance vocabulary rather than inventing a parallel one. artifact-observed and externally-observed keep their existing meaning; human-attested is the one tier that does not fit either, because a human is neither an unverifiable artifact nor an impersonation-proof external system -- it is a named, accountable person.

artifact-observed.proves: The review artifact is internally consistent and structurally valid. It does NOT prove a review happened -- the executing agent can write this file in a path it controls, exactly as EXECUTION-RESULT.json's own core principle already states.
artifact-observed.may_be_promoted_by: a human authority claim of type review-evidence-accepted, bound to this contract, citing a decision record that resolves in decision-log.md and was not itself added or edited within the commit range under verification

externally-observed.proves: A workflow the executor cannot impersonate produced this artifact, PROVIDED all four bindings below are satisfied. A check_run_id alone -- without the other three -- proves only that a CI job of that name completed successfully, not that it ran a review or produced this file.
required_bindings: check_run_id resolves live via the GitHub API and its head_sha/name/status/conclusion match the review entry (reuses Test-CiCheckEvidence's existing binding unchanged)

the check run's own API-attested output carries the SHA-256 digest of the actual EXECUTION-REVIEW.json bytes on disk, recomputed and compared -- never the file's own internal claim about its digest, which would be circular
the workflow file at externally_observed_binding.pinned_workflow_path has, AT THE COMMIT BEING VERIFIED, a content digest equal to externally_observed_binding.pinned_workflow_digest
contract_sha256/base_sha/head_sha recorded on the review entry match the contract and result under verification

human-attested.proves: A named person, not the executor, is accountable for this review. Satisfies Strict identically to externally-observed -- Strict must never become a requirement to purchase a second AI model.
human-attested.attestation_note: reviewer_kind and reviewer are self-declarations. No offline validator can prove who typed a JSON field -- the same standing pmo-config/handoff-policy.json already gives reviewer_kind. What is enforced is that the reviewer is not also the executor named in the execution result, and that any closure this reviewer performs under a human-only category cites a real, resolvable decision record.

externally_observed_binding.note: pinned_workflow_digest is null by default: no adversarial-review workflow has been authored or pinned yet. Until an organization sets this to the real SHA-256 of its own review workflow file, an externally-observed review cannot satisfy Strict on its own -- it fails closed to unverified, the same posture Test-CiCheckEvidence already takes when the gh CLI or a resolvable remote is unavailable. This is deliberate: a partial binding is artifact-observed wearing a stronger name, and must not be sold as more.

closure_policy.$comment: Authority attaches to ROLE (reviewer / executor / human), never to KIND (ai / human) -- an AI serving as a human-attested reviewer's assistant still cannot self-close, and a human executor is still an executor. Enforced by AREV-006, not by prompt.
closure_policy.human_only_close_note: A finding under a human-only category may be marked resolved by a reviewer only when reviewer_kind is human, or closed to false_positive/accepted_risk/deferred by a human citing a decision record -- an AI reviewer may never close a human-only-category finding under any status, whatever the decision reference says. Mirrors HANDOFF-010 exactly.

sees: the approved requirement, scope, and acceptance criteria
the diff between base_sha and head_sha
does_not_see: the executor's chain of thought or persuasion
the narrative fields of EXECUTION-RESULT.json -- written by the actor under review and a claim by this framework's own core principle

preflight.note: axiom verify --preflight runs only the EXEC-* checks that do not require EXECUTION-REVIEW.json to exist yet: contract integrity (EXEC-002), identity match (EXEC-003), scope (EXEC-004), and git-state reconciliation (EXEC-008). It is a flag on the existing verify command, never a new verb or gate, so a review is never spent on a diff whose base does not resolve.
